headline: Cinema Returns to the City
paragraphs: Melbourne — Audiences queued well past the corner last night as the festival opened its doors once more, the projector humming like an old friend. Organisers said the programme had been months in the making, assembled by a committee of students who screened hundreds of submissions in borrowed rooms and late-night video calls.

The opening feature drew applause before its final frame had faded. Several filmmakers travelled from Jakarta, Yogyakarta and Bandung to present their work, and many stayed long after the credits to answer questions from a crowd that refused to go home.

Short films have long been the beating heart of the festival. This year the competition received entries from across the archipelago and the diaspora, ranging from hand-drawn animation to documentary portraits of fishing villages on the north coast of Java.

Critics noted the confidence of a new generation of directors, many of whom shot their films on phones and edited them on laptops. "The tools have changed," one juror remarked, "but the hunger to tell our own stories has not."

Volunteers in printed shirts guided guests between screenings, handing out programmes still warm from the risograph. The smell of ink, said one regular, is part of the ritual — as much a festival tradition as the queue for kopi in the foyer.

Panel discussions throughout the weekend examined distribution, censorship and the role of film schools. A packed afternoon session on regional cinema ran thirty minutes over time, with the moderator eventually conceding defeat to the questions.

The festival will continue through the week with screenings, a filmmakers' forum and a closing night celebration. Tickets for the main screening are expected to sell quickly; organisers advise patrons to book early and arrive with time to spare.

Classifieds — Wanted: one 16mm projector, working or otherwise. Lost: a red umbrella, last seen in Cinema 2 during the late session. Found: a notebook full of storyboards; owner may collect at the front desk.
